public_rationale: The facts he gives as reasons check out. Reuters reported in August 2026 that Anthropic's IPO valuation rests on an internal forecast of $190-200 billion in revenue for 2028. Two summaries of that report say bankers value Anthropic on revenue about two years out, not on current results. That matches his figure and his 'within the next two years'. Anthropic also has very large compute commitments: multiple gigawatts of Google TPU capacity and a $50 billion US infrastructure commitment. 'Cannot afford to slow down' is his reading of these facts and can't be measured directly. One nuance: a Broadcom filing says Anthropic's use of the expanded TPU capacity depends on its commercial performance, so some obligations may scale down if growth slows. On the factual premises, the claim is supported.
limitations: The $190-200B forecast comes from anonymous sources relayed by Reuters, read through secondary summaries.
'Cannot afford to slow down' is a judgment; only its stated reasons were tested.
OpenAI's side of the claim was not tested separately.
2028 revenue is up to about 2.25 years from the post, slightly beyond a strict two years.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI cannot afford a growth slowdown given their compute obligations and valuations that assume, for Anthropic, $190–200 billion annual revenue within two years.

statement.excerpt: Neither of these companies can afford to slow down, in part because of their massive compute obligations, and in part because their massive valuations are based on them being able to pull in, at least in Anthropic’s case, between $190 billion and $200 billion in annual revenue within the next two years.

our_interpretation: The checkable parts are his stated reasons: (a) Anthropic and OpenAI have very large compute obligations; (b) Anthropic's valuation rests on reaching about $190-200 billion in annual revenue within about two years.

'Cannot afford to slow down' is his judgment drawn from those facts. I test the facts it rests on. I do not test whether a slowdown would in fact be unaffordable, which no public evidence can show directly.
'Within the next two years' from September 2026 is read as revenue for 2028, the year the reports name. That is about two years forward.
He describes the state at the time of the post. I use 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-29 so that standing compute deals and the August 2026 valuation reports count.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports before the post show Anthropic's valuation or IPO pricing based on about $190-200 billion of revenue around 2028, and show very large compute commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show Anthropic's valuation rests on a much lower revenue forecast or on current results, or that its compute commitments are small or freely cancellable.
